Kings County New York Inmate Lookup

Finding information about an inmate in Kings County, New York requires knowing where to search and which official resources to use. Whether you're looking for someone in the NYC Department of Correction facilities in Brooklyn or the state prison system, this guide provides step-by-step instructions for conducting a Kings County New York inmate lookup efficiently and legally. Understanding the booking process, bail options, and visitation rules can help you navigate the system during this stressful time.

How to Search Kings County Jail Records

  1. Visit the NYC Inmate Lookup System at https://a073-ils.nyc.gov/nycits/welcome.do and enter the inmate's last name or inmate number. This official database covers all NYC Department of Correction facilities, including Brooklyn's jails.
  2. Check the New York Department of Corrections inmate locator at https://doccs.ny.gov/ if the person may have been transferred to a state prison facility. Use their full name or DIN (Department Identification Number) if you have it.
  3. Call the Kings County Jail information line directly at 718-884-7010 to verify if someone is currently detained and get basic information about their housing unit.
  4. Review Kings County Court Records at https://www.nycourts.gov/courts/2jd/kings/ to find case information, bail amounts, and court dates. Court records are public and often contain details about charges and next appearances.
  5. If the person may be in federal custody, search the Federal Bureau of Prisons locator at https://www.bop.gov/inmateloc/ to confirm they are not held at a federal facility.

Bail Bond Information for Kings County

When someone is arrested in Kings County, the bail system determines whether they can be released before trial. A bail bondsman typically charges a non-refundable fee of 10% of the total bail amount set by the judge. For example, if bail is set at $5,000, a bondsman's fee would be $500. This fee covers the bondsman's service and administrative costs. Many bondsmen in Kings County offer payment plans and accept credit cards or collateral to make bail more accessible to families.

After arrest in Kings County, the arraignment must occur within 24 hours on weekdays or 72 hours on weekends and holidays. At this first court appearance, the judge reviews the charges and decides on bail conditions. Options include release on your own recognizance (ROR), bail set by the court, or remand (no bail). If you cannot afford the full bail amount, a bondsman becomes your solution—they pay the full amount to the court and you repay them the 10% fee plus any collateral required. Having an attorney present at arraignment can significantly influence the bail decision.

Visitation Rules at Kings County Jail

  • Identification Required: All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, or state ID card) before entering.
  • Visiting Hours: General visitation is available Tuesday through Sunday from 1:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Monday visitation is limited. Call ahead to confirm current hours as schedules may change.
  • Dress Code: Wear clean, modest clothing with no exposed midriffs, tank tops, or low-cut tops. No flip-flops or hats are permitted. Avoid camouflage patterns, which resemble inmate clothing.
  • Video Visits: Remote video visitation is available through the NYCLinks system at https://nyc.iconvisits.com. Inmates can schedule video calls with approved contacts on designated days and times.
  • Children Policy: Children under 18 may visit with adult supervision, but facility staff reserve the right to restrict visits if a child's behavior is disruptive.

What to Expect After Arrest in Kings County

  1. Booking: Upon arrival at the Kings County Jail, the inmate enters the booking process where personal information, charges, and physical condition are documented. All personal belongings are inventoried and stored.
  2. Medical Screening: Every inmate receives a health evaluation by medical staff within hours of arrival. This includes screening for infectious diseases, mental health concerns, and chronic conditions requiring ongoing treatment.
  3. Classification: Classification staff assign the inmate to an appropriate housing unit based on security level, behavioral history, and any special needs identified during intake.
  4. Arraignment: Within 24 to 72 hours, the inmate appears before a judge via video or in-person. Bail is set or the person is released on their own recognizance. This is the critical moment for bail bond decisions.
  5. Transfer or Release: After arraignment, the inmate is either released, transferred to another facility, or moved to the general population housing unit in Kings County Jail to await trial.

How to Contact Kings County Jail

Kings County Jail, officially known as the Brooklyn House of Detention and other NYC Department of Correction facilities in Kings County, operates 24/7 to provide information to families and legal representatives. The main inmate information line allows you to verify if someone is in custody and obtain their housing unit. If you need to discuss visitation, commissary accounts, or medical concerns, calling directly during business hours is more effective than relying on the online system. Speaking with a corrections officer or counselor can provide details the automated system cannot.

Frequently Asked Questions — Kings County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Kings County jail?

Use the official NYC Inmate Lookup System at https://a073-ils.nyc.gov/nycits/welcome.do by searching for the person's last name or inmate number. You can also call the Kings County Jail information line at 718-884-7010. The online system is fastest and available 24 hours a day. If the person is not found there, search the New York state prison system at https://doccs.ny.gov/.

How long does booking take in Kings County?

Booking typically takes 2 to 8 hours depending on the complexity of the case and how busy the facility is. During peak times, the process may take longer. The inmate will be available in the system (searchable online) once they complete intake processing, which sometimes occurs before booking is fully finished. You should be able to locate them within 24 hours of arrest.

Can I visit an inmate at Kings County jail?

Yes, visitation is allowed Tuesday through Sunday from 1:00 PM to 8:00 PM, though Monday hours are limited. You must bring a valid government-issued photo ID. Wear modest, appropriate clothing—no tank tops, exposed midriffs, or camouflage. Video visits are also available through NYCLinks if in-person visiting is not convenient. Call ahead or check the facility website for any schedule changes due to facility operations.

What if the person is not in the Kings County jail system?

If your search finds no results in the NYC jails, they may be in the New York state prison system, a federal facility, or already released. Search the New York Department of Corrections database at https://doccs.ny.gov/ and the Federal Bureau of Prisons at https://www.bop.gov/inmateloc/. Contact Kings County Court Records at https://www.nycourts.gov/courts/2jd/kings/ to check court status and discover where they may have been transferred. They could also have posted bail and been released.

How do I send money to an inmate in Kings County?

Inmates in NYC Department of Correction facilities can receive money through the commissary account system. You can deposit funds online through the official NYC corrections website, by mail, or in person at the facility. Funds appear in the inmate's account within 24 hours for online deposits. Ask the inmate for their inmate number and the facility name where they are housed. There is usually a processing fee for deposits. Contact the facility directly at 718-884-7010 for specific instructions on commissary deposits.
